relevance_note: A single-patient case report of a woman with LAD-I and pyoderma gangrenosum: "she suffered from osteomyelitis and sepsis at the age of 13 and she was diagnosed with LAD-1"; no ITGB2 variant is reported for her.
method_note: Hand-extracted; output assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory (values typed from my reading). One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5): diagnosis of LAD-1 at 13, re-evaluated by flow cytometry (Supplementary Table 1) and a migration assay. The paper reports no genetic testing and prints no ITGB2 variant for her, so the variants table is empty (no variant is tied to her) and publications.n_patients_reported is null. The son ('My son will also undergo genetic tests soon'; 'did not present any disorders after delivery') and the husband are neither tested nor affected and get no rows. Age at onset and at diagnosis both come from 'at the age of 13' (onset of non-healing wounds, osteomyelitis and sepsis; diagnosis made then). Age at last evaluation is the stated '20-year-old' at admission; follow-up continued about 5 months more without a stated age. Vital status 'alive' rests on ongoing treatment at last report. Diarrhea and stomachache are attributed by the patient to antibiotics; recorded observed as stated. 'Recurrent minor purulent infections' (Supplementary Figure 1 legend) sets skin or soft tissue infections observed; they imply pus formation, but 'absence of pus formation' is left not reported because no explicit statement addresses it. Not a contradiction but noted: the physician writes 'she had no history of serious recurrent infections' while the supplement mentions recurrent minor purulent infections. PG is described by the authors as an autoimmune-type comorbidity of LAD-1 in general, not stated as autoimmune for her; autoimmune complications left not reported. Normal procalcitonin, immunoglobulins and autoantibodies recorded as excluded abnormalities (D-27); 'the rest of laboratory evaluations' and the normal gynecological examination exclude nothing more specific and get no rows. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: antibiotics (imipenem/cilastatin, linezolid, levofloxacin, ornidazole, fluconazole); surgical debridement; systemic prednisolone and cyclosporine (tapered; prednisolone stopped after 4 months, cyclosporine maintained at 100 mg daily); antimicrobial hydrofiber dressing; physiotherapy, erythrocyte concentrate transfusion, supplementation of albumin, vitamins and minerals; advised to consider HSCT
span: she was treated with many antibiotics, such as imipenem/cilastatin, linezolid, levofloxacin, and ornidazole and fluconazole
Finally, the surgical debridement of the wound was performed, which triggered a clinical deterioration
The therapy was initially started with prednisolone 0.6 mg/kg daily and cyclosporine 4.6 mg/kg daily.

The wound was dressed with an antimicrobial hydrofiber dressing changed once a day because of the large amount of effusion and necrotic tissue. The additional therapy included physiotherapy, erythrocyte concentrate transfusion, and supplementation of albumin, vitamins, and minerals.

Cyclosporine dose has been systematically tapered and prednisolone was discontinued after 4 months of therapy. During the perinatal period and in the postpartum period (5 months from the beginning of the treatment), cyclosporine was maintained at a dose of 100 mg daily (1.7 mg/kg).

The in vitro tests also showed the lack of ability of neutrophils isolated from the patient’s blood to migrate towards chemoattractant
Skin biopsy was not performed because of the patient’s lack of consent for this procedure.
